newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta strengthens further after 84.00/mark break.
newsitem.headline: Peseta strengthens further after 84.00/mark break.

text.p: The peseta strengthened further in late trade on Friday to hover around levels not seen since May after soaring through the key 84.00 per mark level earlier in the session.
By 1615 GMT, the peseta was trading at 83.46/49 per mark after touching 83.45, and compared with late Thursday's levels of 84.08/10.

Traders said a lack of Bank of Spain intervention had allowed the Spanish currency to appreciate past the 84.00 level. The central bank is thought to have been selling pesetas heavily against the mark to support this level since Wednesday.
"After the central bank stopped intervening, the market wanted to push the peseta higher after so much time trapped in such a narrow range," one trader said.
For some months, the central bank has intervened each time the peseta has made an attempt to appreciate through the 84.00 barrier.
Traders said months of built-up pressure to appreciate together with a weak mark and interest rate cut hopes were buoying the Spanish currency.
"The market is clearly betting on a cut in interest rates. With year rates 0.75 points below overnight rates, we are in an unsustainable situation," one trader said.
